title: Unique representative normalization of derived tower evaluation
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal C'$ be small sites with sheaves of commutative rings $R,S$ and a morphism of ringed topoi $(f,c)$, where $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ is left exact and $c:f^{-1}R\to S$. Put $F(M)=f^{-1}M\otimes_{f^{-1}R}S$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Use the module categories and derived localizations $Q,Q'$ of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and strict towers indexed by $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ [def-weil-inverse-system]. Choose universal total left-derived pairs $(L,\varepsilon)$ for $Q'F$ and $(\widetilde L,\tau)$ for its levelwise tower functor. Universality and computation are as in [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class], using the objectwise K-flat flat-term class of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements]. All formulas below include the canonical exact-functor localization identifications. For $n\geq1$, write $e_n,e'_n$ for exact evaluation and its termwise derived functor [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. There is a unique natural isomorphism $v_n:e'_n\widetilde L\xrightarrow{\sim}Le_n$ such that, for every strict objectwise K-flat flat-term tower complex $P_\bullet$,
$$\varepsilon_{P_n}v_{n,QP_\bullet}=e'_n(\tau_{P_\bullet}),$$
using the degreewise identity $e'_nF(P_\bullet)=F(P_n)$. For every $b\geq a$, these comparisons commute with the tower transition:
$$L(d_{b,a})v_{b,M}=v_{a,M}d'_{b,a}$$
on each derived strict tower $M$, where $d,d'$ are the evaluation transition transformations on $M,\widetilde L M$, respectively.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes (dual); parent blueprint completed-pullback invocation, item Step 4 evaluation subargument.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ and $\mathcal T=\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$; write $Q_{\mathcal T},Q'_{\mathcal T}$ for the tower localizations. Evaluation is exact by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] identifies its derived value with termwise evaluation. In degree $q$ both $e'_nF(P_\bullet)$ and $F(e_nP_\bullet)$ are $F(P_n^q)$, with differential $F(d_{P_n}^q)$. For $b\geq a$ the evaluated transition is $F(d^P_{b,a})$ on both sides, since the levelwise functor applies $F$ to each composite transition [def-weil-inverse-system]. Thus these identities include the differentials and every transition, before localization and hence after it.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P_{\mathcal T}$ be the full subcategory of $K(\mathcal T)$ on the complexes whose every level is K-flat with flat terms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements] to the small index category $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$: every complex receives a quasi-isomorphism $P_\bullet\to M_\bullet$ with $P_\bullet\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal T}$, and the levelwise $F$ takes quasi-isomorphisms between such objects to quasi-isomorphisms. The same statement for the one-object identity category gives the corresponding resolving class $\mathcal P_{\mathcal A}$ in $K(\mathcal A)$. Evaluation sends $\mathcal P_{\mathcal T}$ into $\mathcal P_{\mathcal A}$ by its definition. In particular these are resolutions of strict towers, including all their maps.

proof.text: The two resolving classes satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class], by Step 2. Its computation assertion makes $\tau_{P_\bullet}$ and $\varepsilon_{P_n}$ invertible for all $P_\bullet\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal T}$. This applies to the chosen universal pairs: the universal property gives mutually inverse comparison maps between any two universal pairs, since either composite and the identity have the same composite with the universal counit. The comparisons preserve the counits, so invertibility of these components transfers to the specified $\tau,\varepsilon$.

proof.text: Write $U_n=e'_n\widetilde L$ and $V_n=Le_n$. On $\mathcal P_{\mathcal T}$ define $w_{n,P}=\varepsilon_{P_n}^{-1}e'_n(\tau_P):U_n(Q_{\mathcal T}P)\to V_n(Q_{\mathcal T}P)$. It is an isomorphism by Step 3. For a homotopy-category morphism $h:P\to P'$ between good objects, naturality of the two counits of [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] gives, with $H=Q'F$, $H(h_n)\varepsilon_{P_n}=\varepsilon_{P'_n}V_n(Q_{\mathcal T}h)$ and $H(h_n)e'_n\tau_P=e'_n\tau_{P'}U_n(Q_{\mathcal T}h)$. Substitute $\varepsilon_{P_n}w_{n,P}=e'_n\tau_P$ and cancel the invertible $\varepsilon_{P'_n}$. This yields $V_n(Q_{\mathcal T}h)w_{n,P}=w_{n,P'}U_n(Q_{\mathcal T}h)$, so $w_n$ is a natural isomorphism on the full resolving subcategory.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes (dual), combined with categories.tex Tags 04VI--04VK; agent-written evaluation and transition calculation for the completed-pullback invocation in the parent blueprint.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-resolving-representative-whiskering] with $K=H=K(\mathcal T)$, $p=\operatorname{id}$, $q=Q_{\mathcal T}$ and $P=S=\mathcal P_{\mathcal T}$. The category $\mathcal T$ is abelian by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]; its homotopy quasi-isomorphisms have a right calculus of fractions and $Q_{\mathcal T}$ is their localization by [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system]. The required resolving arrows are exactly Step 2, from [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements]. Thus restriction on two-variable functors is fully faithful. It also gives the unary assertion needed here: for unary functors $A,B$ and a transformation on their resolving restrictions, apply fullness to $A\circ\pi_1,B\circ\pi_1$ and the transformation pulled back from the first resolving factor, then restrict the lift along the diagonal. For unary faithfulness, pull two transformations back along $\pi_1$, use two-variable faithfulness, and restrict along the diagonal. Consequently restriction to $\mathcal P_{\mathcal T}$ is fully faithful for functors $D(\mathcal T)\to D(\mathcal B)$.

proof.text: By the fullness established in Step 5, extend $w_n$ and $w_n^{-1}$ of Step 4 to transformations $v_n:U_n\to V_n$ and $z_n:V_n\to U_n$. Their composites restrict to identities, so faithfulness gives $z_nv_n=1$ and $v_nz_n=1$. This proves that $v_n$ is a natural isomorphism with the required normalization. Any other normalized isomorphism $v'_n$ has $\varepsilon_{P_n}v'_{n,Q_{\mathcal T}P}=e'_n\tau_P=\varepsilon_{P_n}v_{n,Q_{\mathcal T}P}$ on good towers. Cancel $\varepsilon_{P_n}$ and use faithfulness in Step 5 to get $v'_n=v_n$.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes (dual), combined with categories.tex Tags 04VI--04VK; agent-written evaluation and transition calculation for the completed-pullback invocation in the parent blueprint.

proof.text:
Fix $b\geq a$ and a good strict tower complex $P$. Let $t=d^P_{b,a}:P_b\to P_a$ and retain $H=Q'F$. Naturality of $\varepsilon$ [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] gives $\varepsilon_{P_a}L(Qt)=H(t)\varepsilon_{P_b}$. The transition transformations from [def-weil-inverse-system], using the termwise localization identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] and Step 1, give $H(t)e'_b(\tau_P)=e'_a(\tau_P)d'_{b,a}$: this is naturality of the target evaluation-transition transformation at the single morphism $\tau_P$ in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal B))$. Therefore
$$\varepsilon_{P_a}L(Qt)v_{b,Q_{\mathcal T}P}=H(t)\varepsilon_{P_b}v_{b,Q_{\mathcal T}P}=H(t)e'_b(\tau_P)=e'_a(\tau_P)d'_{b,a}=\varepsilon_{P_a}v_{a,Q_{\mathcal T}P}d'_{b,a}.$$
Cancel the invertible $\varepsilon_{P_a}$. This proves the transition identity on good towers, including all composite transitions, without making any replacement of their individual levels.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes (dual), combined with categories.tex Tags 04VI--04VK; agent-written evaluation and transition calculation for the completed-pullback invocation in the parent blueprint.

proof.text: Both $L(d_{b,a})v_b$ and $v_ad'_{b,a}$ are natural transformations $U_b\to V_a$. Step 7 says their restrictions to $\mathcal P_{\mathcal T}$ agree. The faithfulness in Step 5 gives their equality on $D(\mathcal T)$, hence at every $M$. For $a=b$, all transitions used are identities and the same calculation reduces to $v_a=v_a$.
